visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

The query's physicochemical profile (low MW, moderate logP, low TPSA, mostly neutral at pH 7.4) is favorable for oral absorption, and no query-specific or close-analog human evidence supports F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule under fed conditions was supplied.
No query-specific food-effect data; fed-state effect is inferred only from structurally related compounds.
Procainamide differs from the query at the para substituent (NH2 vs Cl) and the basic amine (diethylamino vs morpholino), so first-pass and transport behavior may differ.
The only low-F procainamide value is from pigs (C71), and one human patient had indeterminate bioavailability (C58); neither provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for the query.
